cita: Chang et al. (2026). MemCollab: Cross-Model Memory Collaboration via Contrastive Trajectory Distillation.
problema: Memory built from one agent's own reasoning trajectories entangles task-relevant knowledge with that model's reasoning style/biases, so naively transferring it to agents with different backbone models in heterogeneous deployments can degrade rather than help performance.
mecanismo: For each training task, trajectories are collected from multiple heterogeneous-backbone agents; a preferred (correct or strongest-model) trajectory is contrasted against each unpreferred one by the strongest model, distilling (violation pattern, reasoning invariant) discrepancies into normative 'enforce X; avoid Y' memory entries tagged with the producing/failing agent's identity; at inference, task-aware then model-aware retrieval filters the shared bank to entries matching the query's task category and involving the target agent before ranking by relevance and injecting the top-p entries into the prompt.
evaluacion: Evaluated on MATH500, GSM8K, MBPP and HumanEval with Qwen2.5-7B/32B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B-Instruct backbones against Buffer-of-Thoughts, Dynamic Cheatsheet, same-model memory, naive cross-model memory transfer, and self-contrast memory baselines, with ablations on retrieved-entry count, retrieval strategy, and a three-model heterogeneous-source robustness check.
numeros_clave: Qwen2.5-7B + MemCollab raises MATH500 from 52.2% (vanilla) to 67.0% and MBPP from 47.9% to 57.6% (Table 1); naive cross-model transfer (w/ Memory(32B) applied to the 7B agent) instead DEGRADES MATH500 to 50.6% and HumanEval to 34.1% vs vanilla 52.2%/42.7%; top-3 retrieved memories (p=3) found optimal, with performance dropping beyond a task-dependent threshold (Fig. 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The measured finding that naively pooling one backbone's memory as a universal source for a different agent DEGRADES performance (Table 1, 'Direct cross-model memory transfer can degrade performance') is hard evidence for MF's single-source/no-blind-multi-store discipline: memory must be scoped to its valid consumer, not shared blindly.

Distilling contrastive (violation, invariant) pairs into normative 'enforce/avoid' constraints (Sec 2.2) is a concrete consolidation mechanism -- turning disagreement between multiple executions into a durable, reusable rule -- that MF's gotcha-to-recipe consolidation lens could adopt directly.

notes: Ablation on retrieved-entry count Fig. 3 (Sec 3.4); main comparison Tables 1-2 (Sec 3.1-3.2).

cita: Mayank and Nath (2026). Orchestrating Intelligence: A Framework for Dynamic Task Decomposition and Role Specialization in Multi-Agent Generative AI Systems.
problema: Prior multi-agent LLM frameworks rely on static role assignment, brittle ad hoc inter-agent communication, no shared persistent memory across agents, and no principled mechanism for reconciling contradictory outputs from independent agents.
mecanismo: OrchestRAG's orchestration layer decomposes a task into a subtask dependency graph, a Role-Allocation Engine assigns subtasks to agents via competency-embedding similarity, a Shared Episodic Memory (vector-DB backed) lets every agent write acquired findings and retrieve prior agents' findings before executing its own subtask, and a Consensus Arbitrator resolves conflicting parallel outputs via an evidence-weighted vote (competency, confidence, cross-agent consistency) with an LLM-merge fallback.
evaluacion: Evaluated on six benchmarks (HotpotQA, MBPP, BioASQ, WebArena, ALFWorld, SWE-bench) against single-agent GPT-4o, AutoGen, MetaGPT and AgentVerse, reporting task accuracy, tokens/task, wall-clock time and cost/task, plus an ablation removing each of the four architectural components.
numeros_clave: average +23.4pp task-completion accuracy over single-agent GPT-4o and +11.2pp over the strongest multi-agent baseline AgentVerse; 31.7% fewer tokens/task than single-agent GPT-4o (Table 3); ablation (Table 4): removing the Shared Episodic Memory costs -5.4pp vs the full 71.5% average accuracy, removing the Semantic Task Decomposer costs -9.7pp.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The ablation isolates the shared-episodic-memory component's contribution (-5.4pp when removed, Table 4) and attributes token savings specifically to it eliminating redundant retrieval (Sec 5.2), matching MF's requirement that retrieval value be measured per-component.
A full tokens/time/dollar-cost table (Table 3) shows memory-driven token reduction outweighing added orchestration wall-clock overhead, a relevant data point for MF's context-economy lens.

notes: RECONSIDERAR -- published in a low-selectivity outlet (Advanced International Journal for Research), reported deltas (23.4%/31.7%/etc.) are suspiciously round and internally tidy with no code/artifact release; treat numbers with caution.

cita: Wang et al. (2026). MemMachine: A Ground-Truth-Preserving Memory System for Personalized AI Agents.
problema: Existing memory systems (Mem0, Zep) rely heavily on per-message LLM extraction to build memory, which is costly and introduces 'factual drift' through accumulated probabilistic-extraction errors, undermining ground-truth fidelity over long multi-session interactions.
mecanismo: MemMachine keeps raw conversational episodes as ground truth (sentence-level indexed, minimal LLM use) in a two-tier episodic memory (short-term window + long-term store) plus a separately updatable semantic Profile Memory; 'contextualized retrieval' expands a nucleus embedding match with neighboring episodes into a cluster before reranking, and an opt-in Retrieval Agent (router to ChainOfQuery / SplitQuery / direct search) handles multi-hop 'late binding' queries by iteratively accumulating evidence or decomposing fan-out queries.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo, LongMemEvalS (six-dimension ablation across chunking, query-bias correction, context formatting, retrieval depth, search-prompt design, answer-model choice), HotpotQA-hard and WikiMultiHop (Retrieval Agent), and a matched-mode token-usage comparison against Mem0.
numeros_clave: LoCoMo overall score 91.69% (gpt-4.1-mini); LongMemEvalS ablation best 93.0% overall, with retrieval-depth tuning (+4.2%), context formatting (+2.0%), search-prompt design (+1.8%) and query-bias correction (+1.4%) each outweighing sentence chunking (+0.8%); Retrieval Agent accuracy 93.2% (HotpotQA hard) and 92.6% (WikiMultiHop); ~80% fewer input tokens than Mem0 in matched memory-mode comparisons.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The explicit design choice to preserve raw episodes as ground truth and minimize LLM-based extraction specifically to avoid 'factual drift through accumulated extraction errors' (Sec 2.2) is a direct, named instance of MF's fidelity concern about lossy, probabilistically-derived memory.

The ~80% input-token reduction vs Mem0 in matched-mode comparisons and the per-dimension LongMemEvalS ablation isolating which retrieval-stage change buys the most accuracy both directly measure the cost/accuracy tradeoffs central to MF's context-economy lens.

notes: LongMemEvalS six-dimension ablation deltas cited in abstract/Sec 8; Retrieval Agent architecture Sec 5.

cita: Sadowski & Chudziak (2026). Rashomon Memory: Towards Argumentation-Driven Retrieval for Multi-Perspective Agent Memory.
problema: Agents serving multiple concurrent goals must maintain genuinely conflicting interpretations of the same event (e.g. a negotiation concession is simultaneously a 'trust-building investment' and a 'contractual liability'), but current memory architectures commit to a single encoding at write time or a single unified retrieval frame, discarding the alternative framings a different goal would need.
mecanismo: Parallel goal-conditioned 'perspective' agents each maintain their own ontology and knowledge graph and independently decide whether to admit and how to encode each raw observation from a shared Observation Buffer; at query time a Retrieval Arbiter has perspectives propose interpretations, critique (attack) each other's proposals using asymmetric domain knowledge, and computes Dung's grounded argumentation-semantics extension over the resulting attack graph to select one interpretation, compose complementary ones, or surface an unresolved conflict; retrieval frequency is proposed as a stigmergic forgetting/curation signal for encodings.
evaluacion: A controlled proof-of-concept case study (3 goal-perspectives, 8 observations from a synthetic client-negotiation scenario, 4 queries) using Claude Sonnet 4.6 at temperature 0, reporting qualitative encoding-selectivity (Table 1: 13 of 24 possible perspective-observation encodings passed relevance filtering) and a worked query walkthrough rather than a quantitative benchmark.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Treating conflicting interpretations of the same event as legitimately separate, provenance-tagged encodings rather than forcing a single 'true' summary (Table 1, Sec 2.2-2.3) extends MF's fidelity/staleness concern to multi-goal, multi-perspective settings where different consumers legitimately need different framings of the same fact.

Retrieval is framed as negotiation among perspectives rather than search (Sec 2.3), but no quantitative retrieval accuracy is reported (evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA), so it remains weak/neutral evidence for MF's retrieval-measured discipline.

notes: Proof-of-concept only, no quantitative benchmark; encoding-selectivity Table 1 and query walkthrough Sec 2.3, 3 (case study).

cita: Zhang (2026). Deep Researcher Agent: An Autonomous Framework for 24/7 Deep Learning Experimentation with Zero-Cost Monitoring.
problema: Continuous 24/7 autonomous deep-learning experimentation is economically infeasible if the LLM is polled every few minutes to check training progress (est. $50+/day), and long-running agents otherwise accumulate unbounded context that degrades performance and eventually overflows the context window.
mecanismo: A Two-Tier Constant-Size Memory bounds total agent memory at ~5K characters: a frozen, human-authored Project Brief (Tier 1, never rewritten by the agent) plus an agent-maintained rolling Memory Log (Tier 2: milestone 'Key Results' and 'Recent Decisions') that is lossily auto-compacted -- oldest/lowest-priority entries evicted once size/count caps are hit; a Zero-Cost Monitoring phase performs only OS-level checks (process liveness, GPU utilization, log tail) with zero LLM calls during the 90%+ of wall-clock time spent training, admitting new memory via the LLM only when training terminates; a minimal-toolset Leader-Worker multi-agent architecture (3-5 tools/agent) further cuts per-call token overhead.
evaluacion: Real-world sustained deployment across 4 concurrent GPU research projects over 30+ days, reporting operational/cost metrics (cycles completed, best-project metric improvement, LLM cost per 24h cycle, dry-run failure rate) and a memory-size-over-time table validating the constant-size bound, plus a qualitative feature comparison against Claude Scholar/AI Scientist/OpenHands/SWE-Agent.
numeros_clave: Zero-Cost Monitoring reduces estimated cost from ~$1.60/24h (naive polling) to $0.08-0.16/24h (10-20x reduction, Table 2); memory log stabilizes near its 2,000-char cap by day 7 and stays flat through day 30 (Table 4: 312 to 1,834 to 1,978 chars); minimal tool sets cut per-call token overhead by 73%; 500+ autonomous cycles over 30+ days across 4 projects with a 52% metric improvement in the best project (200+ experiments) and 18% pre-training dry-run failure catch rate.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The frozen, human-authored Project Brief (Tier 1) acting as an immutable plan/goal-state the agent cannot rewrite, combined with a bounded rolling decision log (Tier 2, Table 4), is a directly measured instance of MF's plan-state-as-memory pattern with an explicit, quantified size bound.

The Zero-Cost Monitoring design and its measured 10-20x cost reduction (Table 2, Sec 4.3) numerically confirms MF's context/cost-economy principle that expensive LLM calls should be reserved for genuine decisions, not spent polling.

notes: plan_estado=SI reflected in the frozen Project Brief + rolling decision log (Sec 3.3); cost breakdown Table 2-3 (Sec 4.3); memory-size validation Table 4 (Sec 4.4).

cita: Cabrera et al. (2026). Communication Compression Memory Management and Cooperative Reasoning in Multi-Agent Systems.
problema: Multi-agent systems that assume high-bandwidth, uncompressed inter-agent communication become bandwidth- and memory-bound as agent count and task complexity grow, and existing message-compression work treats communication independently from agents' internal memory management, causing redundant re-compression of highly correlated historical data.
mecanismo: A shared learned vector-quantization codebook discretizes each agent's observation into a sparse latent message; a temporal-sparsification step suppresses transmission when the KL-divergence to the last-sent message falls below a threshold, relying on peers' predictive memory instead; a three-tier memory (transient buffer, bounded episodic working memory pruned by a TD-error/novelty/access-frequency utility function, and a consolidated semantic knowledge base of relational graphs/probabilistic rules) evicts low-utility episodic tuples and promotes high-utility ones; a cooperative-reasoning module uses Bayesian belief updates over this compressed shared context to reach joint decisions without full state broadcasting.
evaluacion: Simulated multi-agent environments (a customized StarCraft Multi-Agent Challenge variant and a procedurally generated urban-maze navigation task, 5-50 agents, simulated bandwidth throttling/packet loss/latency) against MADDPG, TarMAC and SchedNet baselines, plus a component ablation removing hierarchical memory management, vector quantization, and adaptive temporal sparsification in turn.
numeros_clave: proposed CCMM-CR reaches 93.8% task completion (vs. uncompressed MADDPG's 94.2%) using only 14.7% of MADDPG's bandwidth (vs. TarMAC 65.4%, SchedNet 35.2%) and a 45MB memory footprint (vs. 250MB MADDPG/TarMAC, 180MB SchedNet) at 14ms reasoning latency (Table 1); ablation: removing hierarchical memory causes transient-buffer overflow and catastrophic forgetting, disabling vector quantization saturates simulated bandwidth with severe packet loss.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table 1's joint bandwidth/memory/latency/accuracy comparison against 3 baselines is a direct, measured cost-vs-quality tradeoff, aligned with MF's context-economy discipline of quantifying rather than assuming the cost of a memory/communication design.

The utility-based promotion of episodic tuples into a semantic knowledge base of 'relational graphs and probabilistic rules' (Sec 3.2) is conceptually similar to MF's consolidation pattern, but is presented only mathematically/algorithmically with no released code, so its concrete transferability is weak/contextual.

notes: RECONSIDERAR -- published in a low-selectivity outlet (IJICTT), 3 of 4 authors share the first name 'Noah', all benchmark numbers are suspiciously round with no variance reported and no code/artifact link is given; treat as unverified and weight accordingly.
